en.why:
The world can be described as a system of interconnected structures of various types and levels. Running through all these structures is one common element — the order of things themselves, being as such. In this light, the present moment is not a coincidence, but a given — the best possible version of what is.

The flow of reality and change cannot be stopped — it is the certainty of passing. Our senses convey only a tiny fraction of available information, and so it can be said that the world arises primarily within ourselves. Roughly 95% of all processes take place beyond conscious control, deep in the realm of the unconscious.

What to do with that 5% of conscious capacity — roughly 48 minutes a day — those gentle flashes, the only thing we truly have? They can be found in the space between emotion and mind (heart), between situation and state (truth), between form and content (meaning). It is the place where a person expands the spectrum of reality grasped by consciousness.

The first step is to name one's why. It is the energy of energies, the inner anchor from which everything else flows. Without being rooted in meaning, direction, or conviction, we cannot endure in the long run — only from why can a meaningful how and a concrete what grow. Why is the meaning, essence, and direction we gladly return to — recollection.
en.noteWhy: I love perceiving the beauty of the world and contributing through who I am. The meaning and strength lie in metaphysical connection. What I am is expressed by the body — and what I am becoming points to the next step.
en.body:
2. The second step can be understood as an attempt to use attention to distinguish precisely the *how* and the *what*. The mind is usually preoccupied with either manifestation — situation, form, action — or with substance — state, content, abstraction. As soon as we perceive one or the other, reality becomes illuminated and can be grasped anew. If we remind ourselves of our *why* (consciousness) and take even a small step in that direction, we accomplish more than we realize in the moment — an expansion of the spectrum. Everything can be placed into the context of reality — integrated through a deliberate merging with our true nature in the *why*.

💡 Tip: Conscious steps can be measured — they are moments when a person is dealing with something (resistance, craving) without being aligned with the full spectrum of reality — senses, thoughts — one's own *why*. On the Today page we distinguish the type of experience, which lets us begin observing what is being experienced, remind ourselves of our consciousness (*why*), and align our direction with reality. That is the win — but now it's about that next small, gentle step forward.

How many times have we acted completely in harmony with the present moment without realizing it? When we enter a state of flow during some activity — that is, pure experiencing of a skill with a clear goal and immediate feedback — consciousness merges with reality quite naturally.

But there is also the mind, with its projection of the conscious component into the human psyche — for example in the form of ego (identification), craving (desire), or will (direction). The mind provides us with forms of knowing: cleverness (practical orientation in the world), reason (analytical thinking), and wisdom (transcending the particular toward the whole). At the same time, it gives us the ability to create on three levels of reality — physical (objective, material, measurable), inner (subjective, immaterial, immeasurable), and social (intersubjective, constituted by agreement rather than fact).

The potential lies in the mind, which is the transcendental component of consciousness. We can be aware of the very process of awareness itself, yet we can equally identify with what is being perceived (the what, the how, the why) — and ultimately we experience the correlate of what we are: a continuous process of becoming. Thought → word → deed → habit → character → destiny.

If we do not identify with the contents of consciousness nor with external circumstances, we remain ourselves — in the most authentic form of ourselves — in harmony with reality, which always works in our favor because it fully merges with our what, how, and why.

💡 Summary: Meditation means relaxed observation of everything that happens, without trying to influence or judge it as "like/dislike." Thoughts and wrong views aren't obstacles but simply things to recognize the moment they appear. Wisdom arises from clarity of mind and reveals things as they truly are. We perceive through the six senses, where the knower and the known merge into experience, returning to them again and again with the joy of discovery rather than judgment. True wisdom means not getting entangled in what happens, accepting things as they are, and having the courage to touch what we fear.
